overview: Cotehele is a Tudor house with medieval roots, set high above the River Tamar on the Cornwall–Devon border, and one of the National Trust’s most atmospheric places. Below the house, a steep valley garden drops down through orchards and woods to Cotehele Quay on the river, and there’s an old mill further along the valley.

It’s a whole estate to explore rather than just a house: rooms full of history, gardens and orchards, riverside paths, and play areas for children. At Christmas it’s known for the enormous flower garland built in the Great Hall.

expect.title: The house
expect.text: Rooms of a Tudor house with medieval roots. It closes in winter for conservation, apart from the Hall and a few rooms opened for Christmas.

expect.title: The Christmas garland
expect.text: Each November gardeners build a huge garland from more than 30,000 dried flowers in the Hall, and it stays up over the festive season.

expect.title: Quay and mill
expect.text: Down by the river, Cotehele Quay and the mill make a lovely walk from the house; a shuttle bus sometimes runs between them.

expect.title: For children
expect.text: There are play areas in the Cherry Orchard near the main car park and at the quay car park, and seasonal family trails.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Paid entry for non-members; National Trust members get in free.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Pay and display for non-members; members park free. Use the upper car parks for the house and the lower one for the quay and mill.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: The café at the quay is closed for building works for now, so check what’s open before you go.

goodToKnow.label: Dogs
goodToKnow.text: Only assistance dogs in the house, orchards and Valley Garden.

goodToKnow.label: By train
goodToKnow.text: The Tamar Valley line runs from Plymouth to Calstock, followed by a 1.5-mile walk along the river and up through the woods.

goodToKnow.label: Access
goodToKnow.text: An all-terrain mobility scooter can be booked for the orchard, parts of the garden and the paths to the quay and mill.

week.text: Cotehele is out on the far eastern edge of Cornwall, so it fits most easily into a day in the Tamar Valley or on your journey in or out. Allow time to walk down to the quay as well as see the house.

a tiny medieval holy well near Callington

tips: Check which parts of the house are open before you go; it closes over winter apart from Christmas.
Wear good shoes: it’s a steep walk down to the quay and back.

setting.note: A historic house plus gardens, quay and riverside paths
